key_insight: The paper proposes a hardware-efficient variational quantum ansatz with an exact closed-form diagonal Fubini-Study metric, enabling metric-aware optimization, time evolution, and Haar-sector sampling without auxiliary measurements or matrix inversion.
engineering_relevance: It can cut two-qubit gate counts dramatically while improving numerical stability for chemistry and dynamical simulations, making variational quantum workflows more practical on near-term hardware.
method: Binary-tree parameterization gives a closed-form diagonal pullback metric.
Supports quantum natural gradient, real/imaginary-time evolution, and exact sector-Haar sampling.
Pruning and reparameterization exploit gauge freedom to reduce circuit size, with optional spin-adapted dressing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reference-level accuracy on small-molecule and Hubbard-quench benchmarks using one to three orders of magnitude fewer two-qubit gates than leading alternatives.
watch_item: The bare ansatz is classically simulable in k for sector-sparse states, so quantum advantage depends on the added dressing and on careful implementation of the pruning/compiler strategy.
paper_title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
